site.name: Alaska Tunnel
overview: Alaska Tunnel is a documented historic mining tunnel in Boulder County's Ward Mining District. Colorado's State Bureau of Mines reported in 1901–1902 that the tunnel at Camp Talcott was actively being driven while the company's other properties also received development work.

Later archival records connect the Alaska Tunnel with the Alaska Gold Mines Corporation and Ward Consolidated Mines Company, preserving a site-specific record of continued mining promotion and development into the twentieth century.

timeline.text: Colorado's State Bureau of Mines reported that the Alaska Tunnel at Camp Talcott was 'driving ahead' while associated company properties received annual development work.
Printed materials preserved by the Carnegie Library for Local History document the Alaska Gold Mines Corporation and identify the Alaska Tunnel in the Ward Mining District.

moreHistory: The Alaska Tunnel belongs to the dense historic underground workings of the Ward district, an important Boulder County gold-mining area.

Modern mineral-locality mapping places the Alaska Tunnel near 40.0733, -105.5072. Remnant uses this documented tunnel locality as the identification point and does not claim that the coordinate is a field-surveyed surviving portal opening.

Archival Alaska Gold Mines Corporation materials survive in the A. A. Paddock collection at the Carnegie Library for Local History, providing direct documentary evidence linking the tunnel to twentieth-century mining promotion in Boulder County.
